answer: Keep one scheme: Lesson 2 = Version 1, the Lesson 3 prokaryote/eukaryote panel = a Version 1 add-on, Lesson 4 = Version 2 (plant cell), Lesson 5 = Version 3, and Lesson 10 = Version 4. Lesson 2 lets learners choose a plant or animal cell, so Lesson 4 should not assume an animal cell. It should tell learners to open to their Version 1 page (the Lesson 2 cell plus the Lesson 3 cheek-cell panel) and draw the plant cell on the facing page. This changes no timings and no KICD outcomes. The Lesson 10 hierarchy stays as Version 4, and its cell, tissue, organ and organ system levels, with the organism as the whole, are untouched.

edits_exact_ok.old: Open to the page facing your animal cell model.
edits_exact_ok.new: Open to the page facing your Version 1 cell model (the generalised cell from Lesson 2, whether you chose a plant or an animal cell, plus the cheek-cell panel added in Lesson 3).

edits_exact_ok.old: Placing the animal cell and plant cell models
edits_exact_ok.new: Placing the Version 1 model (generalised cell plus the Lesson 3 cheek-cell panel) and the Version 2 plant cell model

alternative: Make the Lesson 2 Version 1 cell compulsory as an animal cell so every learner has an animal cell to face the plant cell.

answer: Keep the assessment in Lesson 12 but give every phase a fixed budget that adds to 80 minutes: Predict 7, Observe 14, Explain 12, DQB 12, then exit reflection 5 plus transition 5 plus assessment 25 (35 in all). This is done by running the cold-call round at about 1.5 minutes per student and sorting the DQB into 5 grouped clusters at about 2 minutes each, plus 2 minutes for the driving question. Sections 4 and 5 of the Final Explanation already carry over to a follow-up period, so the KICD outcomes are all still covered.
